result.summary:
The branch was relaunched after the container died: commit 7e666704 held the failing test and probes/junit-before.out, and the worktree held uncommitted edits whose last log line showed Integer.test starting and never finishing. Everything was re-run rather than trusted, including javap on the built classes, and the measurements phase B never reached were taken fresh.

Part one is the repair the brief describes. CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr's bounds become bitLength() <= 31 and <= 63, exact for both signs; FIntLiteral.asNN64 learns to read the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 now keeps, which was forced and measured (junit-codegen-only.out); asNN32's range check, which masked its argument to 32 bits and so accepted everything, is made to mean what it says, which was a decision and not forced — the brief's premise about asNN32 is corrected in the report.

Part one then turned library_tests/Integer.test from green to four failures, all one thing: a radix numeral whose value is outside the annotated signed type, written to mean a two's-complement bit pattern. literals.tex:104-108 gives such a numeral the value of its digits in its radix, and probes r2g and r2h show the interpreter has always refused the idiom, so these are not correct programs the repair broke — they are programs the language does not accept, on which the two paths now agree. The repair reduces divergence and creates none.

The blast radius was enumerated by value in every radix rather than grepped decimally, which is how the radix-16 half was found. Eighteen lines on the compile path, twelve in range and now right for the right reason, six out of range. Five are repaired: ZZ32_MIN and ZZ64_MIN in the prelude (value-identical, in FortressLibrary.fss:703's spelling), twiceHuge in Integer3 and Integer4 (value-identical, same bit pattern written legally, assertions unchanged), and IntegerChoose2, where 3037000500 is bound at ZZ64 so the test exercises the fast/slow boundary its comment names instead of a negative i. Integer.test is OK (27 tests) again; the rung's own test passes.

The batch's one named stop was tested and is not met: the branch in forIntLiteralExpr chooses an overload of FIntLiteral.make, never a type, every numeral still has the flat static type Types.INT_LITERAL, and r2e and p39 show the arithmetic still happening at IntLiteral — it merely starts from the right operand now. That fork is untouched and still open. Three new ledger rows are owed and named in record.md.

differentialsRun: s1, five negative boundary numerals (-2147483649 and -9223372036854775809 at ZZ, -2147483649 at ZZ64, -2147483648 at ZZ32, -9223372036854775808 at ZZ64): walk refuses the ZZ32 line ("RHS expression type Long is not assignable to LHS type ZZ32") and never runs; compiled prints all five correctly. Verdict: the rung's "exact for both signs" holds on the sign it never measured; walk's refusal of a legal ZZ32 declaration is an interpreter defect (rule 4 outcome 2, literals.tex:83-86), a row owed against the interpreter.

s2, NN32 from a string-carried numeral (36893488147419103231, bit length 65, string-carried before this rung as well as after): walk refuses the coercion; compiled raises "Not in range for NN32: 36893488147419103231". Verdict: confirms by measurement the rung's unprobed prose claim that the old vacuous mask accepted the BOGUS sentinel and returned its low 32 bits (0xcafebabe = 3405691582). Quiet-to-loud, an improvement.

s3, the loud-to-quiet case: x = 9223372036854775807; n: NN64 = x + x + 1, whose sum has bit length 64 and so is string-carried by simpleIntLiteralArith.fromBigInteger:31 both before and after this rung. Walk refuses the coercion; compiled prints "-1", asserts equal to the numeral 2^64-1 (true) and unequal to one less (false). Verdict: before the rung this program raised "Error: Not in range for NN64: 18446744073709551615"; the value is now specification-correct but prints signed. See loudToQuiet.

s4, the prelude's own ZZ32_MIN/ZZ64_MIN/MAX bindings read from a component, with independently written comparisons: walk cannot see them (CompilerLibrary is compile-path only); compiled prints -2147483648 and -9223372036854775808 and both assertions (ZZ32_MIN = -2147483647 - 1, ZZ64_MIN = -9223372036854775807 - 1) pass. Verdict: the prelude rewrite -7FFF'FFFF_16 - 1 binds as intended, is value-exact, and is separately pinned by a gated test (AverageTest.fss:98 with :21-23 asserting floorAverage = -1, true only for -2^31).

s5, the two assertions Integer3.fss:99,106 and Integer4.fss:99,106 feed, rewritten from scratch against the new spelling: walk has no BOXPLUS in its library; compiled prints twiceHuge32 -1610612736 and twiceHuge64 -6917529027641081856 and all four BOXPLUS/BOXMINUS assertions pass. Verdict: the corpus rewrite is value-preserving and the assertions assert what they asserted.

s6, CHOOSE at the boundary and at the value the wrap had substituted: walk 4611686016981624750 and 1; compiled 4611686016981624750 and 0. Verdict: the boundary the rung's IntegerChoose2 edit now exercises agrees on both paths and equals i(i-1)/2; the negative argument diverges.

s7, the ZZ32 = -2147483648 line from s1 in isolation: walk refuses it, compiled prints -2147483648. Verdict: isolates the interpreter defect and shows why the team's -max - 1 idiom (FortressLibrary.fss:703) is the spelling that works on both paths, which strengthens the rung's chosen precedent.

s8, CHOOSE at five negative first arguments (-1 with k = 0, 1, 2; -4; -1257966796): walk 1 every time, compiled 0 every time. Verdict: a total divergence at the value IntegerChoose2 was feeding before the rung's repair.

s9 and s10, CHOOSE for k > m >= 0 and the specification's own property: 3 CHOOSE 5 is walk 1, compiled 0; 3 CHOOSE 10 is walk 1, compiled 0; 4 CHOOSE 2 is 6 on both. The property at basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:571-573 at m=3,n=5 gives walk LHS 2 / RHS 1 and compiled 0 / 0. Verdict: rule 4 outcome 2, the specification settles it against the interpreter; cause is the missing k > n guard in interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:287-290, which the compiled path has at nativeHelpers/simpleLongArith.java:187. Outside R2; a row is owed against the interpreter.

p37 and p37a re-run (the rung claims both now agree with walk and measured neither): p37a walk false, compiled false, agrees. p37 walk prints three false lines, compiled dies with "Error: Not in range for ZZ64: 18446744073709551615" from FIntLiteral.asZZ64:75 under CompilerBuiltin.fss:837. Verdict: the record's claim is false for p37; the specification settles it against the compiled run (literals.tex:83-86 requires false) but the fix, comparison over the value rather than at ZZ64, is outside R2's scope, so a ledger row is owed.

library_tests/NN32, NN64 and ZZ compiled and run (the three ungated components holding three of the twelve re-routed numerals, which the rung enumerated and never ran): all three PASS. ZZ.fss matters most because its maxValue: ZZ = FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF_16 was quietly -1 before the rung and is now 2^64-1, and its assertions still hold.

My own blast-radius scan, independent of probes/boundary-numerals.txt: every numeral in every radix in the compile-path prelude and every gated component of library_tests and compiler_tests, valued and range-checked against its annotation. No declaration of the form name: T = <numeral> is out of range for T any more, and the twelve in-range-but-re-routed lines are exactly the twelve the report lists. Widened to the ungated corpora and to every numeral of bit length >= 32 in any position (100 hits), the only out-of-range site left in the tree is library_tests/ChooseTest3.fss:125, which the rung names and leaves for the ledger. No gated compile-path file holds an untyped numeral of bit length >= 64 in a comparison, so the p37 regression does not threaten the gate.
result.loudToQuiet: Yes, in one place, and the rung does not record it. FIntLiteral.asNN64's pre-image is "if (largerVal == null) return FNN64.make((long)smallerVal); throw outOfRange(\"NN64\");" — it threw for every string-carried numeral. simpleIntLiteralArith.fromBigInteger:31, which this rung does not touch, sends every IntLiteral arithmetic result of bit length >= 64 to the string branch, so the transition is reachable without the codegen change and is not confined to numerals. Measured (probes/skeptic/s3): x = 9223372036854775807; n: NN64 = x + x + 1 raised "Error: Not in range for NN64: 18446744073709551615" before and now yields the value 2^64-1 = 18446744073709551615. The value is the specification-correct one: literals.tex:83-86 gives a numeral its exact value and 2^64-1 is inside NN64, and the equality assertions confirm it (equal to the numeral 2^64-1, unequal to one less). The diagnosability cost is worse than the general case because the value prints as "-1" — FNN64.toString is signed (runtimeValues/FNN64.java:20), which is the rung's own proposed row 320 — so the next person gets -1 where they previously got an error naming the true value. Required correction 4 is to record this fact with the probe and tie it to row 320. In the other direction the rung produces three quiet-to-loud transitions, which are improvements: asZZ32/asZZ64/asNN32 now raise where they truncated silently (proposed row 319), asNN32 on a string-carried numeral now raises where it returned the BOGUS sentinel's low half (probes/skeptic/s2), and p37 (see findings).
findings: The recorded failure is genuine and pre-dates the edit: probes/junit-before.out (mtime 23:11) reports "FAIL: ZZ from the 32-bit numeral: -1 should be 4294967295", one minute before commit 7e666704 (23:12:24) and two before CodeGen.java's mtime (23:13:06). It could not have come from a repaired tree — the failing assertion reports the wrap itself. The pass, junit-final.out, is OK (2 tests) on the tree as left.

The test exercises the defect and cannot be satisfied by a constant: every expected value in compiler_tests/IntLiteralWrapRepairR2.fss:41-69 is computed at run time from numerals of bit length 16, 17, 31, 33 and 63, none of which either bound ever mis-read.

The built classes are the diff, checked with javap -c rather than by reading sources: CodeGen.class has bipush 31 and bipush 63 at the two branch tests over BigInteger.bitLength, FIntLiteral.class has asNN32 testing largerVal for null before its comparisons and asNN64 reading largerVal through BigInteger, and both class mtimes are later than their sources'.

The bounds are provably exact, checked arithmetically: BigInteger.bitLength() is ceil(log2(n)) for n < 0 and ceil(log2(n+1)) for n >= 0, so bit length 31 is exactly [-2^31, 2^31-1] and 63 exactly [-2^63, 2^63-1]. The old <= 32 also wrapped negatives, in the other direction (-2147483649 through intValue() came back +2147483647), which the rung never recorded.

The precedent search is complete: grep for bitLength over ProjectFortress/src returns exactly four lines, so there is no fifth site with the defect; interpreter/evaluator/values/FIntLiteral.java:40-56 with bounds at :21-27 is exact for both signs as claimed, and simpleIntLiteralArith.java:31's bitLength() < 64 is numerically <= 63. The rung followed the right one.

The second precedent is stronger than the rung realised: probes/skeptic/s7 shows the interpreter refuses the direct spelling d: ZZ32 = -2147483648, so FortressLibrary.fss:703's -max - 1 idiom is the spelling that works on both paths, not a style choice.

Every file:line in record.md that can be checked, checks out: row 317 is at fortress-gap-ledger.md:328 and 318 is the last row, so 319/320/321 are the next free numbers and nothing is renumbered or moved; the stale-citation correction is right (CompilerBuiltin.fss:557 is now the ceilingAverage comment, the ZZ64 coercion is at :562); the five coercion sites, Misc.scala:467-468, CompilerBuiltin.fsi:370-376, PhaseOrder.java:57 and :142-143, RemoveLiteralCoercions.java:33-53, default_repository/configuration:50-51 and map/spec-to-implementation.md:166 are all as described.

Every specification citation is accurate and from the prose chapters, read in the file rather than from the report: literals.tex:83-86 and :104-108, basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370 and :398-401, literals.tex:132-148. Rule 3 is satisfied.

The cache discipline behind the corpus differential is correct: tmp/phaseD.log shows default_repository/caches/* wiped and the five libraries rebuilt in order before Integer.test was run, so the OK (27 tests) is against the repaired prelude and not a stale jar.

THE RECORD IS NOT ON THE BRANCH: .gitignore:46 is *.out, and git ls-files on the probes directory lists zero of the eight .out files on disk. The recorded failure, the recorded pass, the coupling measurement and the three-way corpus differential exist only in this worktree, and every citation to them in REPORT.md and record.md would dangle in the landed commit.

PROVENANCE UNSTATED: probes/junit-codegen-only.out and the four r2*.compiled.codegen-only outputs are dated 23:17 and were produced by the first container's tmp/phaseA.sh; the second session committed them in a6c0f031 without re-taking them, while REPORT.md says "Everything was re-run rather than read off those logs". The measurement itself is sound — I confirmed the same fact from the pre-image in git diff — but the section headed "What was inherited, and what was re-verified" does not name the exception.

OUTSIDE THE RUNG, from probes it did not write: the interpreter answers 1 for every m CHOOSE k with k > m >= 0 (3 CHOOSE 5 = 1, 3 CHOOSE 10 = 1) against basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:567-568 and the property it states at :571-573, whose two sides come out 2 and 1 on walk and 0 and 0 compiled; cause is the missing k > n guard in interpreter/glue/prim/Int.java:287-290 against the compiled path's guard at nativeHelpers/simpleLongArith.java:187. This is the same missing guard that let verifyChoose(-1257966796+j, 2) pass silently, which is what the rung's proposed row 321 is about.

The asNN32 decision the rung flags is correct and its correction of the brief's premise is right: the old guard masked a long to its low 32 bits and so accepted every value including the BOGUS sentinel, which means it could not throw and what it did was truncate. asZZ32 being left alone is also right, and its accidental dependence on the sentinel's value is honestly recorded.

The three-branch decision is sound and correctly labelled: RemoveLiteralCoercions.java:33-53 does match FIntLiteral.make(I) plus coerce_ZZ32 and the repair does make that substitution sound (it elides asZZ32's range check, safe exactly when the int branch is the ZZ32 range), and the rung says plainly that the optimizer is dormant rather than claiming live behaviour.

The recorded failure exists, pre-dates the edit by its timestamps, and is the wrap itself rather than a generic failure; the test computes every expected value from numerals no branch ever mis-read, so a constant could not have satisfied it. I checked the built classes with javap rather than the sources, and they are the diff. Every specification citation is accurate and taken from the prose chapters. I re-enumerated the blast radius with my own scan rather than reading the rung's: no declaration in the prelude or either corpus is out of range for its annotation any more, the twelve re-routed in-range lines are exactly the twelve reported, and the one site left in the tree is the ChooseTest3.fss:125 the rung names and defers. The prelude rewrite is value-exact and is separately pinned by a gated test the rung did not cite for it, AverageTest.fss:98 with :21-23. I expect the coordinator's gate to be green: no gated compile-path file holds an untyped numeral of bit length 64 or more in a comparison, which is the one shape that now throws. What must change is the record, not the repair. The claim that p37 now agrees with walk is false and was never measured — p37 dies with Not in range for ZZ64 where walk prints false, because rung 6 implemented IntLiteral comparison at ZZ64 — which also falsifies the report's headline that the repair creates no divergence and owes a fourth ledger row. The eight .out files the whole record cites are excluded from the branch by .gitignore:46, so the recorded failure exists only in this worktree, which is the same loss the batch was launched to prevent. The phase-A coupling measurement was inherited from the dead container rather than re-taken, and the report's inventory does not say so. And the rung does not answer the failure-mode question in the loud-to-quiet direction: asNN64 threw for every string-carried numeral before, so an IntLiteral sum of bit length 64 at NN64 went from a named error to the right value printed as -1. Two findings sit outside the rung and are recommended rather than required: the interpreter answers 1 for every m CHOOSE k with k greater than m and at least zero, against the property the specification itself states, and it refuses a legal ZZ32 minimum declaration the compiled path now accepts.

result.precedentSearch: The team solved this three times in VarCodeGen.java and two are right. LocalMutableVar (:451-557) stores a local mutable variable in a MutableFValue cell and routes every read and write through BaseTask.inATransaction() then Transaction.TXRead/TXWrite; MutableTaskVarCodeGen (:609-742) does the same once the variable is captured by a generated task, holding the same cell so the location's identity survives; MutableFieldVar (:202-231) is the wrong one, a bare GETFIELD/PUTFIELD under the author's own "URG, another case of meeting assumptions", and rung 3 followed it. The interpreter stores the same construct transactionally: BaseEnv.putVariable wraps every variable in a ReferenceCell (interpreter/evaluator/BaseEnv.java:595-609; interpreter/env/ReferenceCell.java:26-28, "What the interpreter stores mutable things (fields, variables) in"). The cell is not one option among several: runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:27-28 keys the read and write sets by MutableFValue identity and commits with key.setValue(val) (:231-252), so a cell is the only representation of a location the transaction can hold. I followed the two right precedents.
specCitations: Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:38-42 — all reads and writes in an atomic body appear to occur in a single atomic step with respect to any thread dynamically outside
Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:65-67 — on abrupt completion by throwing, any variable reverts to the value it held before the atomic expression began
Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:96-107 — the chapter's own worked example, a loop body reading and writing a shared counter inside atomic; the shape of the new concurrent test
Specification/basic/memory-model.tex:34-42 — the principle the missing volatile offended: a program must not read values that were never written
Specification/basic/memory-model.tex:69-75 — updates to shared mutable locations are performed with atomic, and a location is shared iff more than one thread can access it
Specification/basic/expressions/bindings.tex:57-59 — assigning a left-hand variable changes the binding for the variable's location
Specification/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:26-30 — an identifier reference evaluates to the value of the name in the enclosing scope and performs a memory read

Specification/basic/components/initialization.tex:12-16,29-30 — all top-level variables and singleton object fields are initialized before their use, which makes a forward reference between initializers a program the language admits
Specification/basic/components/source-code.tex:332-343 — an api's top-level variable declaration is satisfied by the component's, with the same mutability (the citation for the api-export ledger row)
divergences: MutableTopLevelVarInLoop and AtomicTopLevelVar: walk prints PASS at one thread and at four, the unrepaired compiled path fails both. The specification favours walk (atomic.tex:38-42, bindings.tex:57-59), so the compiled side was repaired; the divergence is gone.

P10Field (a mutable object field incremented inside atomic by two threads): walk is exact at 40000 at one thread and at four, the compiled path gives 34481 before and 37831 after. The specification favours walk (atomic.tex:38-42 does not distinguish a field from a variable), and the repair lies outside this rung, so the rung lands and owes a verified ledger row — proposed row 319 in record.md, with the fix location (VarCodeGen.MutableFieldVar:202-231) and what blocks it (CodeGen.java:4323-4342 builds a MutableFieldVar for every field, mutable or not).

A top-level variable exported through an api: neither path is right, but this is not a walk-vs-compiled divergence in this rung's sense — the compiled path fails identically for a mutable and an immutable variable (NoClassDefFoundError: P8Api$shared / P9Api$shared), before and after, so mutability is not the cause and nothing regressed. result.summary:
The rung landed on wip/repair-r1-atomic-static (5 commits off 49ee5e91, all pushed). A mutable top-level variable's singleton field now holds a MutableFValue cell, so reads and writes route through Transaction.TXRead/TXWrite while a transaction is running and a nested code-generation context captures the location rather than a copy — the two right precedents in the same file, not the one wrong one rung 3 copied.
The branch already carried the dead container's two commits. I re-verified rather than trusted, by reverting to 49ee5e91, rebuilding, wiping and rebuilding the cache and re-running; two things did not survive. The inherited concurrent test's comment claimed the gate pins one thread: false for compiler_tests (fastTrack sets none, the fallback is availableProcessors/2), and the base tree fails that test on every run in the gate's own environment — so I corrected the comment instead of weakening the test. The inherited deterministic test was a data race that flaked once in nine runs after the repair; its increment is now inside atomic.
Two regressions were found by probing rather than by the suite. The inherited FValue cell broke a working program, a top-level mutable variable of arrow type, because a compiled closure is not an FValue; the payload is now fortress.AnyType.Any, which also fixes the same pre-existing hole for local mutable variables. The ladder subset over the twenty tests/ programs that declare a top-level variable then caught InitOrderWithMutable, whose initializer reads a variable declared later in the component and so fell into forVarRef's fresh-import path with the old field shape; every top-level binding is now registered before any initializer is generated, and the subset matches the climb's baseline on all twenty files.
Evidence: failure on the base tree (9 of 9 and 6 of 6 runs), pass on the landed tree (27 of 27), the eleven gated atomic programs 22 of 22 both ways, the interpreter agreeing with the repaired path on both tests, and the object-field divergence left as a verified ledger row. The gate is the coordinator's.
